findings.issue: Every new theme-gated panel rule is anchored ONLY on `html.theme--light` / `html.theme--dark`, but <html> never carries a theme class on the new default light boot. `src/App.vue:221` `@Watch('mode')` is NOT `immediate` and `mode` now starts at the new default `'light'` (`src/store/variables.ts:4`, `public/config.json`), so the watcher never fires; `index.html:2` is `<html lang="en">` with no class. Only `App.vue:227` ever writes `doc.className`. Consequences in the default theme: (1) `html.theme--light .v-application .v-card.panel .panel-toolbar-divider { border-bottom-color: ... }` never matches, while the theme-independent rule at Panel.vue:162 sets `border-bottom: 1px solid transparent` — so EVERY panel header loses the hairline divider that HEAD drew via the now-deleted `additionalStyle` inline border; (2) `--panel-header-text` / `--panel-header-icon` are only declared inside those two dead blocks, so `color: var(--panel-header-text)` (Panel.vue:158, 185, 195) resolves as invalid and falls back to inheritance, and the header icon/chevron never get the label-gray ink; (3) `.v-card--link:hover` border override (Panel.vue:141) is dead. This also breaks the convention the other three reskin files explicitly document (dual-gate `html.theme--*` AND `.v-application.theme--*`) — see sidebar.css:19-23 and fonts.css:20-26.
findings.suggestion: Duplicate every theme-gated selector with the `.v-application.theme--light|dark` twin (as sidebar.css/notion.css/fonts.css already do), e.g. `html.theme--light .v-application .v-card.panel, .v-application.theme--light .v-card.panel { ... }`. Add a regression note that `@Watch('mode')` should get `immediate: true` if `html.theme--*` gating is to be relied on at all.

findings.issue: Adding `panel`, `toolbar`, `text`, `border`, `surface`, `sidebar`, `textsecondary`, `textgray` as Vuetify theme keys makes Vuetify's runtime theme service generate `.v-application .<key> { background-color: var(--v-<key>-base) !important; border-color: ... !important }` color-utility classes that collide with real class names used elsewhere in the app. Verified hits: `TheSelectPrinterDialog.vue:192` has a literal `class="rounded transition-swing toolbar py-2 px-2 mb-2 overflow-hidden"` on each printer `<v-col>` — previously an inert token, now a forced opaque `--v-toolbar-base` background plus a fonts.css-pinned `border-color`; `TheSelectPrinterDialog.vue:8` passes `toolbar-color="toolbar"` to Panel, a value that used to resolve to nothing and now resolves to a real palette colour; `dialogs/AboutDialog.vue:2` `<v-tooltip color="panel">` puts class `panel` on the tooltip bubble and relies on notion.css:1209 `.v-tooltip__content { background-color: ... !important }` winning on specificity to avoid a white-on-white version bubble. `fonts.css:96-101` only mitigates `border-color` for `.panel`/`.toolbar`, not the forced `background-color`. This is a global side effect on components outside the reskin scope.
findings.suggestion: Rename the colliding keys so they cannot become class tokens (e.g. `notionpanel`, `notiontoolbar`, `sidebarbg`, `hairline`) or drop them entirely and expose the values only as `--notion-*` custom properties in notion.css; keep the Vuetify palette to the seven standard keys plus `background`/`surface`/`anchor`. Re-grep for `class="\b(panel|toolbar|text|border|surface|sidebar)\b"` and `color="..."` props after renaming.

findings.issue: Default mode flipped dark -> light in three independent places (`public/config.json` `defaultMode`, `src/store/variables.ts:4` `defaultMode`, `src/plugins/vuetify.ts` `theme.dark: false`). This is a behaviour change, not a CSS change: `src/main.ts:74-75` reads `config.json.defaultMode` and sets `vuetify.framework.theme.dark = mode !== 'light'` before Vue mounts, and it uses only the *config* value, never the user's persisted `uiSettings.mode` (which arrives later over the websocket). Existing users who explicitly chose dark therefore now paint the whole app in the light palette first and then flip to dark when `server.websockets.client` delivers uiSettings — a visible wrong-theme flash on every load that did not exist at HEAD (where the three sources agreed on dark). Users with no saved setting silently get a different theme.
findings.suggestion: If the light default is required for the Notion look, persist the resolved mode before mount (read the cached uiSettings / localStorage in `main.ts`) or set `@Watch('mode', { immediate: true })` in App.vue so `html.className` and the Vuetify theme agree from the first paint. Otherwise leave `defaultMode`/`dark` untouched and let notion.css drive the palette only.

findings.issue: The new base rule `body { background: var(--v-background-base, #ffffff) }` cannot beat the inline `style="background-color: #121212"` on `<body>` in `/home/tovi/Documents/GitHub/mainsail/index.html:24`. Only the `html.theme--light body { background: ... !important }` rule (which does carry `!important`, and therefore would override the inline style) can win — and as documented above it never matches on the new light default. Result: the document body stays #121212 in the new light theme (visible on overscroll/rubber-band and behind `#app` before mount). Related leftovers in the same untouched file: `<meta name="theme-color" content="#121212">`, `<link rel="mask-icon" ... color="#d51f26">` and `msapplication-TileColor content="#d51f26"` still carry the old dark/Mainsail-red values while `defaultLogoColor` is now #37352f.
findings.suggestion: Update `index.html`: drop the inline body background (or set it to `#f7f6f3`/`#ffffff`), set `theme-color` to the Notion content background, and refresh the mask-icon/tile colours. Also make the page.css body rule not depend on `html.theme--*` (use `.v-application.theme--*` or a `:root` token) as a belt-and-braces fix.

findings.issue: `html .v-application .v-input--selection-controls__ripple { display: none; }` (notion.css:1041) removes the element Vuetify 2 uses for the checkbox/radio state *and* focus overlay. `v-checkbox` / `v-radio` in Settings therefore lose their only focus affordance: the section-14 `:focus-visible` block (notion.css:1879-1886) only targets `a, button, [tabindex], input, textarea`, and Vuetify's `__ripple` is a sibling `<div>` — so keyboard users on the many Settings toggles now get no visible ring. It also shrinks the clickable hit area around each box (the ripple is `position:absolute; width/height:34px; cursor:pointer`, overhanging the 18px input), which is a usability regression on touch devices.
findings.suggestion: Keep the ripple element for layout/focus and only neutralise the visual state layer, e.g. `html .v-application .v-input--selection-controls__ripple:before { opacity: 0 }` plus `html .v-application .v-input--selection-controls--is-focused .v-input--selection-controls__ripple:before { opacity: 1 }`, or add an explicit `__ripple:focus`/`__input:focus-visible` outline rule in section 14.

findings.issue: The reskin removed the only consumers of three of the custom properties `App.vue:153-156` still computes and writes: `--panel-toolbar-icon-btn-width` (was `Panel.vue` HEAD:123), `--topbar-icon-btn-width` (was `TheTopbar.vue` HEAD:341), `--sidebar-menu-item-height` (was `SidebarItem.vue` HEAD:84) — verified with `git grep "var(--<name>" HEAD` vs working tree; `--panel-toolbar-text-btn-height` was already orphaned before this change. Panel/topbar/sidebar controls are now hard-fixed to `--notion-control-height: 30px` and `--notion-navitem-height: 30px`, so they no longer track `panelToolbarHeight` / `topbarHeight` / `navigationItemHeight` (all `48` in `src/store/variables.ts:132-134`); the sidebar row height is 30px while the mobile workspace row is still bound inline to `topbarHeight` (`TheSidebar.vue:21`) and the `:height="panelToolbarHeight"` prop is still passed to the panel toolbar (`Panel.vue:14`) — so the header content is 48px tall but its buttons are 30px. Four dead `setProperty` writes on every `cssVars` recompute.
findings.suggestion: Delete the four now-unused entries from `App.vue` `cssVars` (and the corresponding `panelToolbarHeight/topbarHeight/navigationItemHeight` import if nothing else needs them), or re-point them: `html .v-application .v-card.panel .panel-toolbar .v-toolbar__content .v-btn { height: var(--panel-toolbar-text-btn-height) ... }` etc. Decide explicitly whether the toolbar height prop should keep driving control size.

findings.issue: The global selected-row rule keys off vue-router's `router-link-active`: `html .v-application .v-list-item--active, html .v-application .v-list-item.router-link-active { background-color: var(--notion-active); ... }` (notion.css:444-465, incl. `__title { font-weight: 600 }` and icon ink). `src/assets/styles/sidebar.css:27-31` explicitly documents the contract "notion.css should drop `.router-link-active` from its selected-row rules" and neutralises the false positive only inside `.sidebar-drawer` (sidebar.css:220-262). The instruction was not implemented. Today the leak is contained — a multiline scan found router `v-list-item`s only at `TheSidebar.vue:18` and `SidebarItem.vue:5` — but any future router-linked `v-list-item` anywhere in the app (settings navigation, printer farm, macro pickers) will render permanently highlighted because `to="/"` matches on every route and these rows do not set `exact`.
findings.suggestion: Remove `.v-list-item.router-link-active` from notion.css:444/450/455/461 and drive selection purely off the exact-match `.active-nav-item` class that `SidebarItem.itemClass` already computes; then the sidebar.css neutraliser block becomes unnecessary and can be deleted.

findings.issue: Token indirection is partly fictional: `--notion-hover`, `--notion-active`, `--notion-border-strong`, `--notion-content-bg`, `--notion-popover-bg`, `--notion-code-bg`, `--notion-text-disabled` all read Vuetify vars (`--v-hover-base`, `--v-active-base`, `--v-border-strong-base`, `--v-content-base`, `--v-popover-base`, `--v-code-base`, `--v-textdisabled-base`) that are NOT declared in `src/plugins/vuetify.ts`, so they permanently resolve to the literal fallback. Dark mode only works because the `.v-application.theme--dark` block (notion.css:105-137) re-declares the same literals by hand. A reader/maintainer will reasonably assume the palette flows through `--v-*` and change vuetify.ts expecting the tokens to follow; they will not. Also two Panel/TheTopbar-referenced tokens (`--notion-text-gray`, `--notion-text-secondary`) depend on `--v-textgray-base`/`--v-textsecondary-base` which DO exist — so the file is inconsistent about which indirection is real.
findings.suggestion: Either declare the missing keys in `plugins/vuetify.ts` (hover, active, border-strong, popover, code, content, textdisabled) so the indirection is honest, or drop the `var(--v-*)` wrapper for the non-existent ones and comment that the literal is authoritative. Note in the file header which `--v-*` vars are guaranteed by vuetify.ts.

findings.issue: All six Roboto `@font-face` rules were deleted (system-font stack), but Roboto is still requested by name in files the reskin did not touch: `src/assets/styles/toastr.css:14` (`font-family: 'Roboto', sans-serif`), `src/components/ui/ConnectionStatus.vue:17,69,115` (inline `style="font-family:Roboto;font-size:16px"` inside SVG text, with NO fallback family), `src/components/panels/Mmu/MmuFilamentStatus.vue:108`, `src/components/panels/ToolheadControls/CircleControl.vue:768,779,785` (`'Roboto-Regular','Roboto'`). Those now silently fall back to the generic sans rather than the Notion stack, so the reskin is incomplete rather than purely tokenised. Meanwhile `public/fonts/roboto-{thin,light,regular,medium,bold,black}.woff2` are now unreferenced but still shipped and PWA-precached (`npm run build` reports 216 precache entries), so the bundle got no smaller.
findings.suggestion: Point the remaining `'Roboto'` requests at `var(--font-notion)` / `var(--font-notion-mono)` (or add a fallback chain), and delete the six orphaned woff2 files from `public/fonts/` in the same change so the asset set matches the new font story.

findings.issue: The component header comment (TheTopbar.vue:322-331) records an explicit contract with the notion.css owner — "disable the Vuetify ripple (hide .v-ripple__container)" — which notion.css never implements (a grep for `ripple` in notion.css returns only `.v-input--selection-controls__ripple` at line 1041). Ripples therefore still animate on the panel collapse chevron (`Panel.vue:24` keeps `:ripple="true"`) and on every Vuetify list/menu surface, contradicting both the documented Notion design and `TheSidebar.vue:23` / `SidebarItem.vue` `:ripple="false"`.
findings.suggestion: Either add the promised global `html .v-application .v-ripple__container { display: none }` to notion.css section 7, or fix the comment and set `:ripple="false"` on `btn-collapsible` so the intent and the implementation agree.

findings.issue: Two selectors in section 15 match nothing in this app: `html .v-application .vue-notification` (notion.css:1898) and `html .v-application .vue-ui-preloader` (notion.css:1894). Mainsail's notification dependency is `vue-toast-notification` (package.json:71), whose DOM classes are `.v-toast` / `.toastr-*` and are styled in `src/assets/styles/utils.css` and `src/assets/styles/toastr.css`; `vue-ui-preloader` appears nowhere in the repo. These look like assumed third-party hooks rather than verified ones, so the app's real toast styling is left on the old Roboto/dark rules instead of the Notion tokens.
findings.suggestion: Delete the two dead selectors and restyle `.v-toast` / `.toastr-*` (utils.css:23,54 and toastr.css) with the `--notion-*` tokens, since that is the surface users actually see for `this.$notify(...)` calls.

findings.issue: `get themeMode()` (theme.ts:24) still returns `?? 'dark'` as the fallback while `defaultMode` is now `'light'`. `themeMode` decides which shipped theme asset variant is loaded — `sidebarBackground-<theme>-light.png` (theme.ts:58), `sidebarLogo-<theme>-light.svg` (theme.ts:75), `mainBackground-<theme>-light.png` (theme.ts:88) — and the CodeMirror colour scheme (`src/components/inputs/Codemirror.vue:91,143`). Any partial uiSettings merge that leaves `mode` undefined therefore renders dark logo/background art and the dark editor theme inside a light Vuetify shell. `src/store/variables.ts:217` (`vzbot`) is the theme that relies on these variant flags, and `vzbot.css` is still consumed via the `themeCss` loader (`App.vue:346-361`).
findings.suggestion: Change the fallback to `?? defaultMode` (imported from `@/store/variables`) so theme asset selection can never disagree with the app default, and grep for any other `?? 'dark'` / `!== 'light'` literals when flipping a default.

findings.issue: The old global `.v-navigation-drawer__content { z-index: 10; padding-bottom: 1em; }` was narrowed to `html .v-application .sidebar-drawer .v-navigation-drawer__content { z-index: 10 }` (sidebar.css:115) and the padding dropped (now notion.css:324). I verified this is safe today — `TheSidebar.vue` is the only `<v-navigation-drawer>` in the repo — but the `z-index: 10` is what keeps drawer content above the `#img` slot background (`v-navigation-drawer__image` is `position:absolute; z-index:0`), and it is now conditional on a component-authored class. Any future drawer, or a theme/override that drops `.sidebar-drawer`, silently renders its nav underneath the sidebar background image (the `vzbot` theme ships `sidebarBackground: { show: true }`).
findings.suggestion: Keep the generic hook (`html .v-application .v-navigation-drawer__content { z-index: 10 }`) for the stacking guarantee and scope only the padding/visual changes to `.sidebar-drawer`, or add the class to the selector's fallback so the layering cannot regress.

findings.issue: Beyond the divider bug, the new header-button block `html .v-application .v-card.panel .panel-toolbar .v-toolbar__content .v-btn { height: var(--notion-control-height, 30px) !important; max-height: ... !important; min-width: 0; ... }` uses `!important`, so it also overrides explicit `height` / `size` props and inline styles on buttons placed in panel header slots across ~60 panels. HEAD's rule was `height: 100% !important; max-height: none`, which let full-height quick-action buttons (e.g. extruder/tool and temperature panel header controls, `MacroButton` instances with `minwidth-0`) fill the 48px bar; they are now clamped to 30px, shrinking the touch/click target while `:height="panelToolbarHeight"` keeps the bar itself 48px tall.
findings.suggestion: Drop `!important` on height/max-height and scope the sizing to `v-btn--icon` and the collapse button only, or read the height from `--panel-toolbar-text-btn-height` so the header buttons track the toolbar's own height prop.

findings.issue: Theme-dependent `html`/`body` background + all `html.theme--light|dark` scrollbar blocks are gated on a class that may never exist. App.vue:221-227 sets `document.documentElement.className` only from the NON-immediate `@Watch('mode')`, and mode now defaults to 'light' (config.json/variables.ts), so for a light-mode user whose stored mode equals the default the watcher never fires and `<html>` carries no theme class at all. `html.theme--light body { background: … !important }` therefore never lands, and index.html's inline `style="background-color:#121212"` wins over the ungated `body { background: var(--v-background-base,#fff) }` — the canvas (root scrollbar gutter, overscroll bounce, pre-mount flash) stays near-black behind a white UI. sidebar.css already uses the correct double gate (`html.theme--x` + `.v-application.theme--x`); page.css does not.
findings.suggestion: Set the page shell ungated: `html, body { background: var(--v-background-base, #fff); color: var(--v-text-base, #37352f); }` (the `--v-*-base` vars are regenerated per active theme on `:root`, so they flip without any html class), duplicate every `html.theme--*` selector with `.v-application.theme--*`, and remove the inline `#121212` body background (plus the stale `<meta name="theme-color" content="#121212">`) from index.html.

findings.issue: `defaultLogoColor` changed from '#D41216' to '#37352f' (light ink) but the logo is a single mode-independent value: TheSidebar.vue:26 and TheTopbar.vue:7 pass it as `:color` and MainsailLogo.vue writes an inline `fill:#37352f`, so in dark mode the mark sits on `--v-sidebar-base` #202020 (1.33:1) and the dark topbar #191919 (~1.2:1) — the printer logo is effectively invisible in dark mode. CSS cannot fix it (inline style).
findings.suggestion: Keep a light/dark pair (e.g. `defaultLogoColorLight '#37352f'` / `defaultLogoColorDark '#d4d4d4'`) and pick by `$vuetify.theme.dark` in the `logoColor` getters, or fall back to `var(--v-text-base)` when the user has not overridden the logo colour.

findings.issue: `--notion-text-gray` (#9b9a97 light) is mapped onto content roles, not just chrome: `.v-label` (810), `.v-messages`/`.v-messages__message` (822), `table th` + `.v-data-table` headers (1276, 1295), `.text-caption`/`.text-subtitle-2`/`.text-overline` (231, 248, 256), inactive `.v-tab` (1474) and the default `.v-icon` colour (1752). findings.issue: `--notion-text-disabled` (#c3c2bf light / #5f5f5f dark) is 1.6-1.8:1 on white and ~2.1:1 on #272727, yet `.text--disabled` (166-168) is used by mainsail for real content, not only disabled chrome: console timestamps + action/debug lines (ConsoleTableEntry.vue:3,27), 'No notifications' (TheNotificationMenu.vue:48), MMU status text, and the connecting dialog's Help button. findings.issue: `--panel-header-text` and `--panel-header-icon` are declared only inside `html.theme--light .v-application .v-card.panel` (line ~128) and `html.theme--dark …` (~136), but consumed by UNGATED rules with no fallback (`color: var(--panel-header-text)` on `.v-toolbar__content`, `.v-toolbar__title`, `.subheading`; `color: var(--panel-header-icon)` on `.panel-icon` / `.btn-collapsible`). rawResult.content: I have completed the audit. Here are the concrete fidelity gaps found:

findings.issue: Spec base type size 14px is never installed. Vuetify's compiled sheet still ships `html { font-size: 16px }` (node_modules/vuetify/dist/vuetify.css:3696) and nothing in fonts.css / page.css / notion.css overrides it: the `html .v-application` typography block (notion.css:139-146) sets family/color/background/letter-spacing but no font-size, and page.css `body` sets no size either. Every element not explicitly pinned to 14px (bare spans/divs in panels, `.subheading` outside toolbars, inline status text, echarts/legend labels) renders at 16px, i.e. one notch larger than the Notion screenshot the tokens describe.
findings.suggestion: Add `html { font-size: 14px }` (or `html .v-application { font-size: 14px }`) in notion.css section 2, next to the existing font-family/color declarations.

findings.issue: Buttons are still UPPERCASE wherever the app adds Vuetify's `text-uppercase` utility. `.v-application .text-uppercase { text-transform: uppercase !important }` (vuetify.css:6981) is !important, so notion.css:588-606 (`html .v-application .v-btn { text-transform: none }`, non-important) loses. Live offenders: src/components/inputs/MacroButton.vue:53,95 (`<v-btn color="primary" class="text-uppercase">`), src/components/inputs/LedEffectButton.vue:6, src/components/panels/Machine/UpdatePanel/Entry.vue:47,82, src/components/panels/Machine/UpdatePanel/EntrySystem.vue:22 — macro buttons and update buttons, the most visible buttons on the dashboard.
findings.suggestion: Add `html .v-application .v-btn.text-uppercase, html .v-application .v-btn .text-uppercase { text-transform: none !important; }` to section 7 of notion.css.

findings.issue: The generic sheet rule at lines 550-557 has specificity (0,9,1) because of its seven `:not()` terms, so it silently beats every later, less-qualified surface rule. `.v-snack__wrapper` is a `v-sheet` (VSnackbar.js:140-141 merges `VSheet.options.computed.classes`), so the upload snackbar gets `background-color: var(--notion-surface)` + `color: var(--notion-text)` instead of the declared dark pill at notion.css:1228-1234 (`--notion-snackbar-bg` #191919 / #ffffff text). The `--notion-snackbar-*` tokens are dead code, and `.v-snack .v-progress-linear__background { rgba(255,255,255,.25) }` (line 1248) is now invisible on a light pill. Same trap hits `.v-tabs.v-sheet` (line 1449, intended transparent).
findings.suggestion: Extend the `:not()` chain with `.v-snack__wrapper`/`.v-tabs` (or add `!important` to those two component rules).

findings.issue: Notion popover elevation is lost on two floating surfaces because the shadows are not !important. (a) `.v-snack__wrapper { box-shadow: var(--notion-shadow) }` (line 1232, (0,2,1)) loses to Vuetify's `.v-sheet.v-snack__wrapper:not(.v-sheet--outlined)` (vuetify.css:27806, (0,3,0), Material elevation-6 shadow) — the menu/dialog shadow spec is not applied. (b) `html .v-application .v-picker { box-shadow: var(--notion-shadow) }` (lines 1679/1683) is non-important and VPicker's root element is `v-picker v-card` (VPicker.js:79), so the earlier `html .v-application .v-card { box-shadow: none !important }` (line 513) cancels it — the file's own header comment (line 22-23) promises pickers get the Notion shadow.
findings.suggestion: Mirror the pattern already used for `.v-menu__content` (line 1151) / `.v-dialog .v-card` (line 1188): give the snackbar and picker shadows `!important` plus enough specificity.
